findings.evidence: grep for `PureBraidGroup` in code/TauCeti returns only the definition at Basic.lean:235 and its mention in the module docstring (line 45); no other occurrence in the repository.
findings.fix: Add `mem_pureBraidGroup_iff : b ∈ PureBraidGroup n ↔ permHom n b = 1` and a witness showing it is nondegenerate, e.g. `sigma i ^ 2 ∈ PureBraidGroup n` (permHom sends it to `swap ^ 2 = 1`) together with `sigma i ^ 2 ≠ 1` via `exponentSum` (`ofAdd 2 ≠ 1`).
findings.issue: `PureBraidGroup n := (permHom n).ker` has no consuming theorem and no nondegenerate witness anywhere in the PR or repo — not even a membership characterization — so nothing exercises the predicate it introduces.

findings.evidence: Basic.lean:238 and :256; the only lemma about the map is `castSuccHom_sigma` (:261), which computes it on generators and says nothing about injectivity.
findings.fix: Either prove `Function.Injective (castSuccHom n)` (or drop it and) reword both docstrings to describe the map without claiming injectivity, e.g. "the homomorphism B_n →* B_{n+1} sending σ_i to σ_i".
findings.issue: `castSuccGen` is documented as "the natural generator-embedding" and `castSuccHom` (line 256) as "the natural strand-inclusion group homomorphism"; injectivity of B_n → B_{n+1} is a nontrivial theorem and is neither stated nor proved here, so the docstrings claim more than the file establishes.

summary: The Artin presentation, exponentSum, permHom and castSuccHom are all mathematically faithful; I could not break any statement. Two gaps: PureBraidGroup is an orphan definition with no consuming theorem or nondegenerate witness, and the castSucc docstrings assert an embedding/inclusion that is never proved injective.
